script: [serious] Australia sent the army to fight birds. And the birds won. In 1932, about twenty thousand emus were tearing through wheat farms in Western Australia. So the government sent soldiers, led by Major Meredith, with machine guns. The emus scattered. The guns jammed. The trucks couldn't keep up. In the end, by Meredith's own count, his men fired nearly ten thousand rounds, and he claimed under a thousand kills. Even that number is disputed. Within weeks, the army was pulled out. Farmers built fences instead. It's remembered as the Great Emu War. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number twenty-one. A new file every day.
